historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta travelled to Yala in 1332 AD during his travels in the East African coast. He described it as a prosperous town and a center of commerce and trade between various African and Asian communities.

In the late 15th century, Yala was ruled by the Swahili kingdom of Mwito, which was a major power in the eastern African coast. The kingdom controlled the trade routes between the Indian Ocean and the interior of Africa, making Yala an important center of commerce and cultural exchange between Africans and Arabs.
